Whether scorer stores exactly five ground-truth relevant IDs or a larger relevant set.

metric_interpretation.conventional_ap5: sum over predicted ranks r=1..5 of precision_at_r multiplied by membership(prediction_r, relevant_set), divided by min(5, number_of_relevant_items).
metric_interpretation.prediction_order: Matters: an isolated relevant prediction at rank1 contributes more than at rank5 when other ranks miss.
metric_interpretation.actual_order: Conventional binary MAP uses ground-truth set membership, not target item preference ranks. Reordering the same five correct predicted IDs yields AP=1 when those five comprise the relevant set.
metric_interpretation.caveat: This describes conventional binary MAP and our implementation; actual competition scorer implementation is unavailable.

reassessment.all_distinct_watched: A useful broad-viewing task, but now clearly unconfirmed as official preference target. Do not call it matched Kaggle ground truth.
reassessment.top5_proxies: Text makes top-five preference proxies a motivated sensitivity analysis, not proof of actual hidden-target construction.
reassessment.threshold80: Participant-reported heuristic/target account only. Official excerpt neither confirms nor refutes it. Keep provenance distinct.
reassessment.prior_local_scores: Remain valid measured scores for their documented proxy. Do not relabel previous results as official-MAP estimates.

recommended_bounded_analysis: Freeze existing predictions and compare all-relevant versus top5-by-completed-airing-count and top5-by-overlap-seconds targets.
State threshold, aggregation, tie handling and fewer-than-five-truth treatment for each proxy.
Show whether model ranking changes across target proxies; two Kaggle points cannot identify the true preference formula.
Do not select a label definition merely because it yields a higher absolute local score; proxy difficulty changes.
